feature_profiles.no_claim: The default RaptorQ ConfigLoader is INI-style and is not evidence for TOML parsing.
This profile does not expose ATP CLI or atpd configuration.
The cli feature does not compile the atpd binary unless atpd-daemon is also enabled.
Source inventory is not a real daemon start, reload, failure, or precedence E2E.
Cargo manifest transformation is an internal audit-tool surface, not an operator runtime-config API.

toml_surfaces.read_behavior: Read entire file through EnvReader, deserialize to an intermediate all-optional model, then apply to a fresh RuntimeConfig.
load_all attempts daemon policy then local config; user_config is never loaded; read and parse failures are swallowed and the layer remains absent.
toml_surfaces.write_behavior: Pretty TOML is written directly with create_dir_all plus fs::write; not atomic, no fsync, comments and input ordering are not preserved.

toml_surfaces.read_behavior: Secure variants constrain the requested path to an explicit base; compatibility variants pass the path directly and emit a tracing warning.
toml_surfaces.write_behavior: Pretty TOML is written directly with create_dir_all plus fs::write; not atomic, no fsync, comments and input ordering are not preserved.

toml_surfaces.read_behavior: Missing file returns defaults. Existing read or parse failure propagates from load_daemon_config, but the start path catches any loader error and falls back to defaults.
Parses root and member Cargo.toml files into toml::Value, then performs named dependency, feature, workspace, dev-dependency and target mutations.
toml_surfaces.write_behavior: Writes pretty generated shadow manifests directly; comments and original ordering are not preserved.

adjacent_surfaces.behavior: Test-only TOML serialization round-trips LossMatrix and FallbackPolicy; no production parse or write call exists.
Legacy-harness test-only TOML properties operate on MockRuntimeConfig rather than any production config type.
Public ConfigLoader is an INI-style line parser with six sections and 33 exact keys; it rejects unknown sections and keys and is not TOML.

low_to_high: RuntimeBuilder::with_env_overrides when called after TOML construction
precedence_contracts.caveat: Precedence is method-call order, not an enforced global layer manager; calling with_env_overrides later always mutates the current builder.
A user_config path and User save scope exist, but load_all never loads user_config. Failed daemon/local reads and parses are silently treated as absent layers.
First-run creates the file and upgrade reads, rewrites, backs up, and restores it; this is persisted state, not a multi-layer configuration.

low_to_high: AtpdConfig::default when file is absent or start catches a load error
precedence_contracts.caveat: Start flags can enable selected booleans but cannot disable file-enabled values; reload does not apply every listener-affecting change without restart.

low_to_high: deterministic shadow-manifest mutations selected by the tool
precedence_contracts.caveat: This is transformation order, not user configuration precedence.

io_and_security_contracts.path_policy: No base-directory confinement; EnvReader owns file access.
Environment-derived base paths reject traversal, excessive length, controls, and relative Unix paths; the local file remains ambient-current-directory relative.
io_and_security_contracts.permissions: OS defaults; no explicit restrictive mode

io_and_security_contracts.path_policy: Secure public variants require an explicit base; first-run and upgrade call compatibility variants without a base.
io_and_security_contracts.permissions: OS defaults; no explicit restrictive mode

io_and_security_contracts.path_policy: Repository/internal-tool paths and resolved workspace members.

error_contracts.distinction: BuildError custom message includes the requested path and source I/O error.
BuildError custom message prefixes failed to parse TOML config and preserves toml parser detail.
BuildError reports semantic builder failures such as a NUL thread-name prefix after parsing.
ConfigError::FileRead and ConfigError::FileWrite retain path and source error when directly returned.
ConfigError::Parse retains path and toml::de::Error, but manager load methods swallow it.
ConfigError::InvalidScope retains the rejected scope string.
ConfigError::PathSecurity distinguishes explicit secure-path validation failure.
CLI error text prefixes Failed to read config file.
CLI error text prefixes Failed to parse config file and includes toml parser detail.
The start path converts any loader error into a warning and default config rather than a failing exit.
anyhow context distinguishes manifest read, parse, shape, transform, and shadow write failures.

known_gaps.finding: Capability registry and API map route TOML to src/config.rs and src/bin/asupersync.rs, but neither owns a toml call; the real owners are inventoried here.
No integration test exercises RuntimeBuilder::from_toml with a real file path.
There is no checked-in runtime TOML example; ignored rustdoc refers to nonexistent config/runtime.toml.
The legacy metamorphic TOML tests use MockRuntimeConfig, not live config types.
AtpConfigManager defines a user config path and User save scope but load_all never loads user_config.
AtpConfigManager silently swallows missing, unreadable, and malformed daemon/local config instead of preserving the public ConfigError distinctions.
atpd start catches every config read/parse error and starts with defaults; other atpd subcommands propagate the same error.
Typed TOML structs do not deny unknown fields, including unknown security-adjacent keys; this conflicts with the registry's stated fail-closed unknown-security-field invariant.
ATP/install/shadow-manifest writes are direct fs::write operations without tempfile, fsync, rename, rollback, restrictive permissions, or comment/order retention.
No application-level input byte, nesting, string, array, table, or work limit is enforced for TOML documents.
The portfolio config-profile fixture enables config-file but exercises only the non-TOML RaptorQ ConfigLoader and never RuntimeBuilder::from_toml[_str].
ADR language says all config tables and fields are optional, but AtpInstallConfig and most AtpdConfig tables and fields are required by observed serde behavior.
Operator-facing TOML read, parse, validation, path, and fallback diagnostics have no stable ASUP error codes and no proven secret-redaction boundary.

Versioned JSON model APIs, canonical conversion paths, and cross-format source tests now exist for runtime, ATP command/install, and atpd, but focused executable confirmation has not run; ATP persisted writers remain TOML and physical atomic I/O is still A4-owned.

Programmatic ATP overlays built with struct update from AtpConfig::default inject Some defaults for unrelated keys and override lower-priority layers; the existing test_config_precedence currently observes Auto instead of expected SyncTree.
